meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national jurisdiction; commercial courts and notary regime established by the Code de commerce and décret n° 78-78)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pending UBO tax-residency identification, the precise treaty matrix must be crystallized; the principal French instruments for cross-border investors include the France–United States Double Taxation Convention (1967, as amended by Protocols of 2006 and 2009), the France–China Double Taxation Agreement (2013, in force since 2015), the France–United Kingdom Double Taxation Convention (2008, as amended), and the relevant EU free-trade arrangements applicable to e-commerce goods such as CETA (provisionally applied) and the EU–Japan Economic Partnership Agreement.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Code monétaire et financier (CMF), Articles L561-1 et seq. and R561-1 et seq. (AML/CFT customer due diligence and beneficial ownership); Code de commerce, Article L123-3-2 and R123-151 et seq. (UBO declaration transmitted to the Registre National des Entreprises); EU Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers of funds; EU Regulation 269/2014 and EU Regulation 881/2002 (restrictive measures); Décret n° 2018-1055 of 27 November 2018 and implementing orders concerning the RNE and UBO register.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (corporate existence) of any non-EEA corporate shareholder or ultimate corporate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or corporate registry of the shareholder’s jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the originating state’s competent authority or, for non-Hague jurisdictions, French consular legalization; followed by certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the French incorporation representative and registered-office/domiciliation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder’s or UBO’s jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, then sworn French translation by a translator listed on a court-approved roll

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each director, legal representative and each UBO identified under Article L561-2-2 CMF
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the person’s country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized or professionally certified copy; apostille/legalization and certified French translation required where the French incorporation service or the receiving bank expressly requests full authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Evidence of residential address of each UBO (bank statement or public utility bill, issued within the immediately preceding three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original or certified copy; apostille generally not required for private utility statements, but notarized certification is customary when the document supports a French AML/KYC file

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory, documented and auditable screening of all directors, legal representatives, shareholders holding directly or indirectly at least 25% of the SAS share capital or voting rights, and all UBOs against: (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List and EU Regulations 269/2014 and 881/2002; (ii) OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, necessary for USD settlement through Stripe and correspondent banking; (iii) UN Security Council sanctions and FATF high-risk jurisdiction lists; (iv) French domestic restrictive measures and alerts transmitted by Tracfin and the Direction Générale du Trésor; and (v) national and third-country PEP databases, including negative-news review and source-of-wealth verification for any PEP-linked incorporator. Screening must be completed before acceptance of any shareholder advance or incorporation payment, must be refreshed within three business days of a sanctions-list change and must be repeated at each UBO event.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités d’entreprises of the Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle (INPI), creation module and RNE availability search; accessible at https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr and https://data.inpi.fr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is the official language of the Republic (Constitution, Article 2). The SAS statutes must be drafted in French. The corporate name may contain foreign words, but it must be transmissible in Latin script and, where the UBO’s home language uses non-Latin script, a French phonetic transliteration must be included in the RNE filing. Any supporting public document must be translated into French by a sworn translator. France does not operate a formal statutory name-reservation system; however, the selected corporate name must pass an availability check against the RNE/INPI business database and the EUIPO trademark database before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Because France has no paid name-reservation right, the legal representative shall, at least 30 days before the formal incorporation filing, complete an RNE/INPI and EUIPO search, hold the chosen domain name and, where commercially justified, file a French or EU trademark application. If INPI or the competent registrar rejects the proposed corporate name or the complete RNE registration on grounds of identity, similarity or infringement of prior rights, the incorporator may (i) file a corrective resubmission through the Guichet unique; then, if maintained, (ii) lodge an administrative-legal challenge before the tribunal de commerce for refusal of registration, or before the tribunal judiciaire for trademark infringement claims, within 30 days of receipt of the rejection notice, accompanied by a counsel’s availability opinion and any consent letter from the prior rights holder.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for an ISIC 4791 e-commerce SAS, provided the company contracts its siège social with a registered commercial domiciliation company (domiciliataire) under Article L123-11-3 of the French Commercial Code. A bare post-office box without a written domiciliation contract and managed mail-forwarding service is not accepted as a registered office by the RNE or by payment service providers. For tax substance purposes, the company must retain the domiciliation contract, keep board-decision records at or accessible from the registered office, and avoid mere letterbox operations.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated unannounced on-site inspection risk: below 10% per year for a low AML-risk online retail SAS with no statutory license, no cash-on-delivery sales and a compliant domiciliation contract. The likelihood rises to approximately 25–35% per year if the tax administration opens a substance review under Article L16B of the Livre des procédures fiscales, or if the domiciliation address hosts a concentration of unrelated companies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public database access is free; attorney time estimated at two professional hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the statutory legal announcement in an authorized legal gazette (Journal d’annonces légales)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Publisher tariff aligned with DILA information and legal-administrative guidelines

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RNE incorporation filing through the INPI Guichet unique, including the commercial registry (greffe) registration fee for an SAS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: INPI / RNE and competent greffe through the Guichet unique
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Government-administrative filing fee schedule applicable to SAS creations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC, PEP, UN/EU, OFAC and French domestic sanctions screening for all identified UBOs and statutory representatives
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance provider and French legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-beneficial-owner database compliance package; non-statutory market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, consular legalization and certified French translation of the UBO identification bundle (passports, corporate good-standing certificate, power of attorney and address evidence)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Origin-country competent apostille authority, French embassy or consulate where required, and sworn translator
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Public consular fee schedules plus sworn-translation page rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office domiciliation agreement and managed mail handling for the first twelve months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of approximately USD 75 per month for SAS domiciliation with mail scanning and retention

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Code de commerce (French Commercial Code), articles L. 227-1 et seq. (Société par Actions Simplifiée)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce du siège social
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte de constitution de la société
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of 1 euro; no escrow account required for SAS
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The undersigned initial shareholders and directors of the proposed Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) unanimously resolve: (1) to subscribe to the entire initial share capital of one (1) euro represented by one (1) share of one (1) euro nominal value; (2) to adopt the registered office at [Insert Full Address], France; (3) to appoint [Full Name] as Président and [Full Name] as Directeur Général with full powers of representation; (4) to authorize immediate filing of incorporation documents with the competent registry and opening of a corporate bank account. This resolution is adopted on [Date] and shall remain in force until further notice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) – primary tax authority and taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; customs and export excise administration: Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (DGDDI) – portal: douane.gouv.fr (DELTA/GUN e-customs clearance system)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity must (i) register the SAS with the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) via the Institut National de la Statistique et des Études Économiques (INSEE) to obtain the obligatory identification numbers SIREN/SIRET; (ii) obtain the French VAT intra-Community number ('numéro TVA intracommunautaire' = FR + two-digit automated key + SIREN) by filing form CERFA for VAT registration with the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE) having territorial jurisdiction, or, where no French fixed establishment is created, with the DGFiP non-resident taxation unit (Service des impôts des particuliers non-résidents / unité TVA des non-résidents); (iii) alternatively, a non-established EU or non-EU e-commerce seller may cover qualifying distance sales and imports of consignments not exceeding EUR 150 through the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) regimes, thereby avoiding a full French VAT registration; (iv) for intra-Community zero-rated supplies, the SAS must present the customer's valid EU VAT identification number and file the EC Sales List (état récapitulatif de chiffre d'affaires) in the VAT return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation – the Société par Actions Simplifiée (SAS) is compulsorily subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) at its own statutory entity level; headline IS rate 25% for fiscal years opened from 1 January 2022, with the reduced 15% rate applicable to the first EUR 42,500 of annual taxable profit for eligible SME taxpayers (turnover below EUR 10,000,000 and paid-up capital held at 75% by individuals); no automatic pass-through is permitted for an SAS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France does not apply a US-style 'check-the-box' system; however, (i) a small SAS satisfying the statutory conditions (no more than five shareholders, at least 50% of rights held by individuals, turnover ≤ EUR 10,000,000) may elect for partnership-class fiscal transparency for a maximum of five fiscal years under Article 239 bis AA of the Code Général des Impôts (CGI), with the election filed with the DGFiP before the end of the opening fiscal year; (ii) transparent partnerships may conversely elect corporate taxation under Article 206-3 CGI; (iii) hybrid entity mismatches are neutralized by the French hybrid mismatch rules transposing EU ATAD (Articles 209 VIII, 210, 238 bis CGI), and a foreign hybrid branch/entity is treated as French-taxable only to the extent its profits are not deductible elsewhere; (iv) group consolidation (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI is available as a statutory election to a 95% parent for income tax pooling of French subsidiaries.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA – Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) administered by DGFiP under Articles 256 to 289 CGI, with EU Directive 2006/112/EC implementation
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: France applies no domestic 'small trader' franchise threshold to non-established sellers: a non-established taxable person must register from the first taxable transaction or apply the IOSS for imported consignments ≤ EUR 150 / Union OSS for remote B2C supplies. For taxable persons established in another EU Member State, French VAT accounting is triggered by the EU-wide EUR 10,000 annual distance-sales threshold (intra-Community distance sales of goods and B2C electronically supplied services) once exceeded in France. Domestic 'franchise en base' thresholds (EUR 85,000 for sales of goods / EUR 85,000 for retail distance sales where the franchise has been reformed; EUR 37,500 for services) apply only to French-established small businesses and are not relevant to an SAS carrying on commercial e-commerce.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is implementing the statutory e-invoicing/e-reporting reform (Finance Act 2023, end-of-2022 ordonnance): from 1 September 2026 all B2B transactions involving large and mid-sized French taxable persons must issue structured e-invoices (Factur-X/CII/UBL or EDI) cleared through the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a Partner Dematerialisation Platform (PDP) delivering validation and data transmission to DGFiP; from 1 September 2027 the obligation extends to SMEs and micro enterprises. B2C and cross-border sales require e-reporting (données de transaction) to the PPF in near-real time via API, including the customer's country, payment details and VAT accounting codes. No blockchain-style digital stamping is used; compliance relies on structured-data electronic clearance, digital signature integrity, and archiving of invoice datasets for a 6-year period. For B2C e-commerce of portable power products, the VAT invoice/credit note dataset (invoice number, issue date, supplier/customer identifiers, VAT rate, VAT amount, payment method) must be transmitted continuously.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exonération) is available strictly for (i) direct exports of tangible goods physically shipped or transported by the seller or its forwarding agent to a destination outside the European Union, under Article 262-I CGI, subject to proof of physical removal from EU customs territory within the statutory time limits; (ii) intra-Community supplies of goods dispatched to a customer identified with a valid EU VAT number and taxable in another Member State, under Article 262 ter-I CGI (subject to EC Sales List filing and the 'assujetti revendeur' rules); and (iii) services directly connected to exported movable goods (transport, handling, carriage and ancillary services) treated as territoriality-excluded under Articles 259-A/B CGI. Solar portable power equipment sold via the Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS): imported consignments ≤ EUR 150 benefit from a VAT-remitted-at-import flow, the seller collecting French-appropriate import VAT in the IOSS return and no separate export zero-rating being claimed at dispatch; above EUR 150, normal customs import VAT and the use of the free circulation customs declaration apply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation – DAE) lodged electronically in the DELTA/GUN system, including export customs procedure code and destination country
Commercial invoice issued under Article 242 nonies A CGI with mandatory VAT details
Bill of Lading (B/L), CMR consignment note, Air Waybill (AWB), or postal/courier shipment proof evidencing physical dispatch from France/EU territory
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank payment proof (attestation de rapatriement des recettes d'exportation) evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a bank
Packing list, transport insurance certificate, and, where applicable, the customer's valid intra-Community VAT number plus the EC Sales List and Intrastat supplementary declarations
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to joint DGFiP/DGDDI audit scrutiny: if documentary evidence of physical exportation or intra-Community dispatch is insufficient, the exempt VAT is reversed ('rappels de TVA'), with monthly late-payment interest of 0.20% (intérêt de retard, Article 1727 CGI) and the full statutory penalty regime: 10% for untimely filing (Article 1728), 40% for intentional inaccuracy (Article 1729-a), 80% for corrective dissimulation or fraudulent activity (Article 1729-b) or for invocation of fraud/abus de droit; false or fictitious export declarations also trigger criminal customs fines and penalties under Articles 413 quinquies and 414 of the Code des Douanes (exclusion from export privileges, amende of up to EUR 50,000 and imprisonment up to three years, confiscation of goods and means of transport); the retroactive clawback period is the standard 3-year tax reprise period (Article L. 176 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales and Article 354 of the Code des Douanes), extended to six years in cases of undisclosed EU or third-country arrangements, and increased export refund/restitution claims may be prosecuted as customs fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (French central bank operating within the Eurosystem of the European Central Bank); prudential supervision and AML/CFT licensing are performed by the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR); balance-of-payments statistics and financial relations with foreign countries are administered by the Banque de France and the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) under the Code monétaire et financier.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on current account and capital account under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and Articles L151-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier. France maintains no exchange control approval for inbound or outbound remittances for a French-resident SAS. Practical hurdles are limited to (i) statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the Banque de France for cross-border transactions above EUR 750,000; (ii) customs declarations for physical movements of cash or equivalents of EUR 10,000 or more; and (iii) dividend withholding tax of 25% on outbound profit distributions under Article 119-bis of the French General Tax Code, reduced or eliminated under applicable double tax treaties or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (participation of at least 5% held for 24 months). No central bank 'fair return' or capital authorization certificate applies to ordinary equity injections or trade-related payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no mandatory surrender, no compulsory conversion ceiling, and no statutory repatriation deadline on export proceeds. Export contracts may be invoiced and settled in EUR or any freely negotiable currency, and foreign-currency receipts may be retained indefinitely in French bank accounts. All commercial and financial transactions between a French resident and a non-resident exceeding EUR 750,000 must be reported statistically to the Banque de France through the presenting bank, using the official balance-of-payments nomenclature; cash movements of means of payment equal to or exceeding EUR 10,000 must be declared to customs at the border.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank (Crédit Agricole S.A.)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium-to-High for ACPR-licensed French electronic money institutions and payment institutions (e.g., Qonto, Shine, MANSA) that offer SEPA/Instant SEPA, SWIFT multi-currency accounts, and remote onboarding; viability is conditional on their inability to provide escrow blocking, documentary trade finance, bilateral FX/derivatives credit lines, or complex treasury architecture, hence a Tier-1 bank relationship remains the anchor. UK-based and offshore EMIs lost EU passporting rights after Brexit; they may operate only through an EU-licensed branch, under PSD2 'agency' arrangements, or on a restricted 'reverse solicitation' basis, and they should be limited to ancillary collection/payout flows rather than primary treasury settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under Articles L561-1 et seq. of the Code monétaire et financier, the bank must identify the legal representative, directors, signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners before opening the account. French Tier-1 banks generally require at least one physical interview of the SAS president or a French-resident authorized signatory; remote video-KYC is accepted by some institutions for EEA-resident individuals and by most digital-only banks, but for non-EEA directors the de facto standard is a physical appearance before a French notary or consulate, or a written power of attorney with apostille, certified French translation, and verifiable instruction chain. The bank may re-verify beneficial ownership at any time, and the absence of a French registered office or French-established signatory materially raises the onboarding refusal risk.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or shareholder resident in a non-cooperative, high-risk, or sanctioned jurisdiction; mismatch between corporate substance and KYC profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled passport and proof of residential address older than 3 months; source-of-wealth file comprising tax declarations, employment contracts, and financial statements; statutory declaration of beneficial ownership under Article L561-2-2 of the Code monétaire et financier; two reference letters from regulated EU banks; certified French translations of all corporate documents; and a written commercial rationale letter with an entity relationship diagram.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce model using aggregated third-party payment processors (Stripe, Affirm BNPL) that generate commingled, high-volume, low-ticket flows difficult to trace to underlying trade.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant and sub-merchant agreements with the PSPs; access credentials to the live dashboard showing transaction-level reconciliation; annualized volume and country distribution reports; PSP AML and internal control policies; PCI-DSS attestation; refund/chargeback policy and chargeback history; French VAT (TVA) registration certificate; and a segregation certificate confirming the PSP's account is distinct from the SAS operational account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection originating from an offshore holding company, a family trust, or unlisted vehicle without visible economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain from the offshore entity to each individual beneficial owner; certificate of incorporation and register of shareholders; corporate board resolution approving the contribution; bank statements showing the source-of-funds provenance; a funds-flow chart covering at least two upstream levels; audited or accountant-reviewed financial statements of the contributing entity; and evidence of tax residence with confirmation of no adverse FATF status.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated French SAS with no credit history, no French office other than a registered address, and projected turnover disproportionately high relative to capital.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latest K-bis extract; articles of incorporation with capital structure and authorized signatories; realistic three-year business plan with P&L and cash-flow projections; signed supply or purchase agreements in the solar portable power sector; proof of the commercial website and Stripe/Affirm onboarding status; a lease or service contract for a physical French establishment; and a letter of engagement from an expert-comptable (statutory accountant) attesting to the accuracy of the projected accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The shareholder capital contribution is routed by SEPA Credit Transfer for EUR-denominated remittances or by SWIFT MT103 with the mandatory Unique End-to-end Transaction Reference (UETR) for non-EUR transfers, using the Banque de France balance-of-payments purpose code for direct investment (code 'EC', apport en capital) and an unambiguous beneficiary reference citing 'FR_SAS libération du capital social'. The French receiving bank must be a licensed credit institution; funds are first credited to a blocked capital escrow account (compte d'apport), held until the constitutional or capital-increase formalities are completed, then released to the operational account upon presentation of the notary certificate of deposit and the updated K-bis extract. For the SAS, the capital amount is freely set in the articles and cash contributions must be released in accordance with the statutory regime applicable to simplified joint-stock companies. Any single transaction at or above EUR 750,000 must be covered by the Banque de France statistical declaration submitted through the presenting bank; the bank also verifies the source of funds and the tax residence of the contributor for French withholding reporting.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements for the procurement of portable battery generators and solar panels, predominantly from Asian manufacturers, are executed through (i) SEPA Credit Transfer or Instant SEPA for EUR payments up to EUR 100,000; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for international wire transfers in USD, EUR, or CNY with the correct Banque de France balance-of-payments code for imports of goods and the underlying commercial invoice attached; (iii) documentary irrevocable Letters of Credit (SWIFT MT700/MT707 in accordance with UCP 600) for high-value or credit-based orders, issued or confirmed by the French bank with the supplier's bank as advising/negotiating bank and documents comprising commercial invoice, packing list, Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, and inspection certificates; (iv) documentary remittance (documents against payment / documents against acceptance) for lower-risk, low-value repeating suppliers; and (v) direct RMB disbursements through the French bank's cross-border RMB clearing arrangement or CIPS-correspondent channel provided the beneficiary maintains an onshore RMB account. All FX conversions are booked through the bank's dealing room, with the euro leg always cleared through TARGET2 and domestic payments through the French retail clearing system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and EUR/GBP with tenors typically up to 12 months (extendable to 24 months), documented under the FBF (Fédération Bancaire Française) master agreement for foreign exchange and derivatives (Convention FBF devises) and confirmed by SWIFT MT300.
FX swaps combining a spot transaction and a forward leg for short-term liquidity alignment between EUR, USD, and CNY balances without altering the underlying commercial exposure.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for medium-term conversion of USD or CNY payable streams into EUR, including interest-rate alignment where the SAS enters a floating-to-fixed structure with the same credit institution.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or non-convertible currencies (e.g., INR, IDR, PHP, and TWD when physical delivery is restricted) settled in EUR or USD against the prevailing fixing rate, documented under the FBF convention and subject to the bank's FX credit line.

Vanilla FX options and zero-cost collars (range forwards) to protect import margins within a bounded exchange-rate band without upfront option premium; the option premium on purchased structures is paid in EUR, and net selling of options is restricted to covered hedge positions.

OTC FX and interest-rate derivatives are subject to EMIR trade reporting to a registered trade repository; the SAS, as a non-financial counterparty below the clearing threshold, benefits from the EU clearing exemption for OTC FX and interest-rate derivatives, while maintaining the obligation to promptly confirm all transactions under the FBF master agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: SAS annual accounts approval (ordinary general meeting or written consultation of shareholders)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate records; minute book kept at the registered office; no separate filing until accounts are deposited
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of the balance-sheet date; a court may extend the period for a further six months upon justified request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct fine; any shareholder may apply to the tribunal to appoint an authorized agent to convene the meeting; late approval automatically postpones the RCS accounts deposit and triggers registry penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Liasse fiscale – annual corporate income tax return (form 2065-SD and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – French tax administration via EDI-TDFC electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end: file on or before 3 May of the following year; for other year-ends: within three months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under CGI art. 1728: 10% of assessed tax if paid within 30 days of formal notice; 40% after that deadline; 80% in cases of deliberate concealment; plus 0.20% per month of late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 April following the tax year, with monthly VAT returns already filed during the year; specific deadlines apply for fiscal-year taxpayers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% for ordinary late filing after notice, rising to 10%, 20%, or 40% depending on response and concealment; 0.20% monthly late-payment interest.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts with the Commercial Register (dépôt des comptes annuels au RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce / RCS, filed through the INPI Guichet Unique e-formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the annual shareholders' approval; the approval itself is due within six months of the balance-sheet date (e.g., by 30 June/31 July for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,500 for a natural person and EUR 7,500 for the legal entity; court-ordered injunction; repeated failure to file in two consecutive years can lead to strike-off from the RCS and possible judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner (UBO) register and RCS dossier annual verification process – corrective filing only if changes occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No calendar-year confirmation is required; initial UBO declaration was made at formation and any change must be filed within 30 days; the company must verify the RCS data before depositing the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission or false UBO declaration is punishable by fine up to EUR 15,000 for entities and imprisonment/fines for managers; non-updated dossiers can be rejected at the annual accounts filing and are a factor in registry strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) must be appointed for an SAS when, at the end of two consecutive financial years, at least two of the following thresholds are exceeded: total balance-sheet assets greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover (exclusive of VAT) greater than EUR 8,000,000; average number of employees greater than 50. Audit is also mandatory for companies that control or are controlled by entities themselves subject to audit, or where specific provisions or independent requirements impose it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The SAS individual statutory accounts must be prepared under French GAAP (PCG – ANC Regulation 2014-03) and filed in French and euros; IFRS as endorsed by the EU applies only to consolidated or listed-group accounts when required.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not operate an annual UBO reconfirmation filing for an SAS. The UBO declaration is filed at formation and updated only when a change occurs; any share transfer changing percentage ownership must be reflected in the securities transfer register and, if the natural-person beneficial owners change, submitted to the RCS within 30 days. The RCS dossier is refreshed at each annual accounts deposit, and the registry can compare the capital structure against the declared UBO at that time.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of members and securities transfers (registre des mouvements de titres)
Minute register of shareholders' meetings and written consultations (minute book)
Register of president's and board decisions and reports
File of UBO declarations and supporting identification evidence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120–650 per year for virtual office/domiciliation services in France; USD 1,000–3,500 per year for a professional registered-agent package including secretarial support and filing coordination.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 below the mandatory audit thresholds; USD 8,000–28,000 for a statutory audit when the EUR 4m/8m/50-employee test is exceeded, depending on sales volume and inventory complexity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit for qualifying SMEs (annual turnover below EUR 10 million); Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% of eligible prototype costs up to EUR 400,000 for SMEs; Young Innovative Enterprise (JEI) exemption up to 100% for the first 3 years and 50% for years 4-6; the 3.3% social contribution on corporate income tax raises the aggregate top effective burden to 25.825% where the tax payable exceeds EUR 763,000.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_policy_note: French law grants an indefinite loss carryforward, annually capped at EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; a one-year carryback (report en arrière) is limited to EUR 1,000,000 and becomes a credit usable over 5 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (Résultats de l'entreprise) with annexes 2050 to 2059-SD; mandatory electronic filing via the DGFiP 'Espace Fiscal des Entreprises' (EFI/TelePAC) portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; four quarterly prepayment installments (acomptes) are due on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, each equal to 25% of the prior-year corporate income tax; the final balance of IS is payable with the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a fiscal year ending 31 December, the e-filed annual return and final tax payment are due on 3 May of the following year; for any other fiscal year-end, the return must be filed no later than three months after the closing date (e-filing grants a 15-day supplementary extension).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable result (bénéfice fiscal) after statutory accounts and French GAAP-to-tax adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute from audited French statutory accounts; reinstate non-deductible expenses under Article 39 CGI and adjust for foreign-source income reservations under the territoriality system.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses deducted against current-year profits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only the statutory cap: EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above EUR 1,000,000; keep detailed loss-pool schedules available for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits carried forward and reclassification of the research and innovation credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the CIR/CII certificates and justify the arm's length accounting treatment of intra-group sales of solar portable power equipment; unused CIR is refundable after three years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net deficit of the year (déficit fiscal)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should be aware that the SAS's deficit is trapped at the entity level; no flow-through to a foreign parent is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax due (montant de l'IS)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 25% to the taxable result (15% on the first EUR 42,000 if the SME conditions are met); add the 3.3% social contribution where the base IS exceeds EUR 763,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic 10% increase in assessed tax; 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days of a formal notice; 80% for fraudulent manoeuvres or abus de droit. Late payment: monthly 0.20% late-payment interest plus a 5% penalty where the tax is not settled within 30 days of the notice. Missing annexes attract a fixed fine of EUR 150 per document; persistent default triggers taxation d'office under Article L. 68 LPF.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2257-SD (Annexe relative aux prix de transfert) — transfer pricing reporting return, filed electronically on the same EFI/TelePAC portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same deadline as Form 2065-SD: 3 May for a December 31 year-end and no later than three months after the fiscal year-end in other cases.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the worldwide group, ownership percentages and intercompany commercial flows
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the ultimate parent and the French nexus of the SAS; required to demonstrate compliance with Article 57 CGI and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of cross-border purchases, royalties, management fees and e-commerce platform charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory where cross-border related-party flows reach EUR 100,000 per year; for a direct online retailer, disclose logistics and warehousing fees paid to the foreign group.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section V – Transfer pricing method chosen
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selection of the methodology and the comparability analysis
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: TNMM with an operating-profit margin is typically the most defensible method for online retail; the report must identify benchmarks and the tested party.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Fine of EUR 15,000 (or 5% of the value of undocumented transactions if higher) per year; the fine rises to EUR 100,000 per company and per year after a formal notice to produce the documentation; the tax administration may additionally re-price the transactions and re-assess French taxable income.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding under Article 119 bis (2) CGI for dividends paid by a French SAS to non-resident corporate shareholders; 12.8% final withholding for non-resident individuals under the prélèvement forfaitaire unique (PFU); 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate parent resident in the EU or in a treaty territory holds at least 10% of the share capital for a minimum holding period of two years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty-reduced rates, the non-resident recipient must deliver to the French paying agent, before the first payment or at the latest by the prescribed filing date, Form 5000/5001 (individuals) or Form 5050/5051 (companies) together with a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC / attestation de résidence fiscale) issued by the tax authority of the residence state and containing the specific treaty reference; for EU parent-subsidiary exemption, Form 5003 must be filed proving the 10% shareholding and the 2-year holding commitment; the French SAS must keep the certificates in its records for six years for audit verification; where the relief is not granted at source, the recipient may file a claim for refund (réclamation) before the end of the calendar year following the year of collection under Articles R*196-1 and L. 190 LPF.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding of 25% under Article 182 B CGI on payments for services and for the use of intellectual property exploited in France (reduced from the former 33.33% statutory rate); 0% on qualifying royalties paid to an EU associated company under the Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) where the recipient holds at least 25% for at least two years; treaty rates generally range from 0% to 10%. Interest: no domestic withholding tax applies to interest on bank loans paid to non-residents (Article 125-3 CGI); however, interest or deemed interest paid to entities in non-cooperative States (CTHS) is subject to a 75% withholding tax, and certain hybrid arrangements attract a 50% rate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 — full Master File and Local File are compulsory where the French company or the consolidated group reaches this annual turnover threshold; a simplified transfer pricing declaration (Form 2257-SD) is required for every French entity with cross-border related-party transactions of at least EUR 100,000 per year; a Country-by-Country Report is mandatory for groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces economic substance through the general anti-abuse rule (abus de droit, Article L. 64 LPF), the sham-entity doctrine (société fictive) and the concept of gestion de fait; treaty relief is denied where the SAS lacks genuine management and operational substance or where the principal purpose of the structure is treaty shopping (PPT under the Multilateral Instrument); France transposed the EU minimum taxation directive (Pillar Two, Directive 2022/2523) applying a 15% global minimum top-up tax to low-margin groups; consequently, a solar portable power e-commerce SAS must maintain real substance in France: permanent premises, operational staff, local decision-making and French-side logistics and inventory.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing a false Form 2065-SD, concealing taxable profit from online solar equipment sales, deducting fictitious invoices, or moving profits to a foreign affiliate to avoid French corporate income tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 1741 CGI: fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; aggravated cases (international dimension, organised group) carry fines up to EUR 3,000,000 and imprisonment up to 7 years, together with publication of the judgment, confiscation of assets, exclusion from public tenders and denial of tax treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SAS president or acting manager who orchestrates the fraud is personally criminally liable; under Article L. 267 LPF the administration may hold the de facto manager jointly liable for the company's tax debts; the court may impose a travel ban (opposition à sortie du territoire), attachment of personal assets and an interdiction de gérer for up to 15 years.
